title: Burned by People Too Many Times
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece addresses the cumulative toll that betrayal and disappointment take on leaders over a career, and argues against letting that history harden into distrust. The author acknowledges that every long-tenured leader accumulates episodes where a team member acted in bad faith, and that this naturally breeds caution. But the piece insists that becoming 'callused' after enough bad experiences is a form of surrender. The argument frames extending trust, even after being burned, as a core obligation of leadership rather than a naive choice. Ultimately the piece reframes resilience to disappointment as a defining leadership skill rather than a personal failing.
points: Leaders who lead people over many years will inevitably be exploited or disappointed by some of them.
Becoming 'callused' toward all team members because of a few bad actors punishes the many for the sins of the few.
Extending trust and optimism, even after repeated disappointment, is framed as an explicit obligation of leadership, not naivete.
Team members can't reach their full potential without feeling their leader's trust, giving a leader's guardedness a direct performance cost.
quotes: Lead enough people over a period of years, and the odds are you will experience many instances where a team member acts in bad faith or so inappropriately the relationship must come to an end.
With each new incident, it is common for leaders to ask themselves whether it is truly worth it to let their guard down and completely trust the people they lead.
The obligation of every leader is to presume the best of people and to act accordingly. Anything less makes the job of leadership untenable for everyone involved.
Becoming callused to the instances and people where this trust is misplaced is surrendering to the few and privileging that experience over the many.
Because you can rise above those instances and maintain the optimism and trust in people required to lead them. That's why you are the leader.
